messages:
sam: Quick heads-up — after onboarding rerank-v5-ptq we see a small but repeatable NDCG@10 gap (~1.2%) vs fp16 on our long-doc benchmark. Not massive but above our rollout threshold.
anya: Which slices show the gap? any dataset-specific pattern?
sam: Mostly docs with multiple relevant passages and queries where the gold passage is >60% into the doc.
mike: Could be the concat/truncate window selection. Are we still centering the window at the start?
sam: Prod runtime currently truncates head-first: anchor + doc tokens truncated from the tail. In eval we do a shingled passage approach (64-token overlap) and score passages independently. Different passage selection leads to different candidate pools.
yuki: Hmm. That's a mismatch. Also I wonder if PTQ increases sensitivity to small semantic shifts caused by passage boundary differences.
anya: Can we do a quick ablation to attribute the delta: 1) fp16 passthrough with concat-trunc, 2) ptq concat-trunc, 3) ptq shingled. Want to see chunking vs quant contribution.
sam: Running three arms now. Commands: 
```
python eval.py --strategy=concat_trunc --max_total=512 --model=rerank-v5-fp16 --out=fp16_concat.csv
python eval.py --strategy=concat_trunc --max_total=512 --model=rerank-v5-ptq --out=ptq_concat.csv
python eval.py --strategy=shingled_passages --passage_len=256 --overlap=64 --model=rerank-v5-ptq --out=ptq_shingled.csv
```
infra-bot: job started: rerank-onboard-2189991110 (run=4452).
mike: Also collect per-query NDCG difference and paired-bootstrap CI (we need uncertainty).
sam: Will do. Early peek on 2k queries: chunking-only flips account for ~0.6% NDCG loss, quant-additional ~0.5%, overlap small.
anya: So both matter. For mitigation: long-term we should align eval to prod. Short-term could we add a model-level calibration head or rescale scores for PTQ?
mike: Score rescaling might patch some bias but not passage selection issues. Another approach: token-dropout augmentation during fine-tune or calibration to make the model robust when context shifts across boundaries. We tried token-dropout on LM fine-tune before, worth a shot for rerankers.
yuki: I like token-dropout + truncation-jitter augmentation in eval to catch edge cases. Also propose adding a paired-bootstrap gate: new model must show NDCG no worse than baseline with 95% CI overlap on prod-like concat_trunc sample.
anya: Agreed. Also curious if changing runtime to perform a cheap pre-tokenization alignment (pad/truncate doc to preserve likely gold window) would help without blowing tokens. Maybe a heuristic: if doc length>1024 and gold-likely-position>50% then bias window back by 128 tokens. But that needs gold-estimation heuristics.
mike: That's a bit heuristic-y and brittle. Prefer fixing eval + augmentation and then model retrain/calibrate.
sam: For immediate action items: 1) upload flips CSV + token offsets to s3://rerank-artifacts/2189991110/flips.csv, 2) add paired-bootstrap script to eval harness (I'll PR), 3) try token-dropout fine-tune run (small) and test.
yuki: I'll start the paired-bootstrap script — use 1000 bootstrap samples, compute delta NDCG@10 and output p-value.
infra-bot: job completed: rerank-onboard-2189991110 (run=4452) status=success. artifacts uploaded.
anya: Once we have CI numbers, we can decide whether to block the rollout or require a small calibration PR.
sam: Uploading examples of top1 swaps and a short visual showing token clipping points. ETA 25m.
mike: Thanks. If token-dropout helps, we can add a small PTQ-aware fine-tune step in onboarding pipeline. That may remove a large part of the quant-amplified flips.
yuki: Good plan. I'll sync with infra about running a Dedicated canary with concat_trunc eval enabled to measure actual latency/token cost impact if we move eval->prod alignment.
anya: OK — tagging @mike @sam for followups. :thumbsup:
